doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

chapter: Becoming an audio man and DJ
title: Encyclopedic memory and school grades
summary: His memory works across subjects; he nearly let grades slip for jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Wow. You know I’m curious, does this encyclopedic knowledge of yours, when you were in high school did it work in other venues too?
Oh sure man. What do you want to know about American history?
Do you want me to do the vice presidents for you?
I don’t know, how much tape do we have?

Yes I’ll talk you to death. That’s another problem with this memory. I’ll talk you to death. Guilty as charged. I did well in school and in fact my jazz interests were saved because I was ready to have my academic career plummet, you know, due to my complete devotion towards jazz, which merges head and shoulders over anything else in my junior high school years. It makes me both an outlaw and an outcast. And I felt that the dues that this was going to cost me would be catastrophic in terms of the goody two shoes, straight ahead, you know, super high grades college thing. And you know I had a 99 average and I stopped going to school, stopped doing my homework, came and took the test and all of a sudden it went down to 97. So the memory came in handy.
